library.original:

Evidence: Average of average math = sum(average math scores) / count(schools).
library.explicit: Start from each `satscores` record; combine it with each `frpm` record for which California Department Schools (`satscores.cds`) equals Central Directory System Code (`frpm.CDSCode`) (compared as text, character by character), one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); keep only the records for which district name (`frpm.District Name`) matches the pattern 'Riverside%' (ASCII letters match regardless of case; % stands for any run of characters and _ for one); group the kept records by school name (`satscores.sname`) and charter funding type (`frpm.Charter Funding Type`); each group gives one result row; keep only the groups for which A ÷ B is greater than 400; for each result row, return (1) school name (`satscores.sname`); (2) charter funding type (`frpm.Charter Funding Type`). Here A is the sum of average SAT math score (`satscores.AvgScrMath`) in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); B is the number of records in the group whose California Department Schools (`satscores.cds`) is not missing.
library.gold_sql: SELECT T1.sname, T2.`Charter Funding Type` FROM satscores AS T1 INNER JOIN frpm AS T2 ON T1.cds = T2.CDSCode WHERE T2.`District Name` LIKE 'Riverside%' GROUP BY T1.sname, T2.`Charter Funding Type` HAVING CAST(SUM(T1.AvgScrMath) AS REAL) / COUNT(T1.cds) > 400
